subtitle: Neural and Spectral Noise Removal
tagline: Reduces steady background noise, hum, hiss, clicks, and clipped peaks while protecting the voice, with a learnable noise print and a focus band for targeted work.

body.lead: TB Noise Remover reduces room tone, air conditioning, fans, hiss, and other steady background noise while protecting the voice. Its hybrid engine combines neural speech enhancement with spectral restoration, and switches to the spectral path whenever the neural path cannot run.

body.p: One `REDUCTION` control moves from natural cleanup to strong suppression. Separate switches treat specific problems, such as rumble, mains hum, hiss, digital whine, clicks, and clipped peaks, so each one is processed only when it is present. `LEARN NOISE` captures a noise print from a noise-only passage, and Focus Band concentrates the reduction on a frequency range you select on the analyzer.

ul: `BASIC`: the main hybrid cleanup for ambience, air, and room residue
`LEARN NOISE` captures 0.75 seconds of noise-only audio as a noise print; `CLEAR PRINT` returns to adaptive cleanup
Focus Band concentrates the reduction on a frequency range selected on the analyzer
Targeted switches: `LOW RUMBLE`, `50 Hz HUM`, `60 Hz HUM`, `HISS`, and `DIGITAL WHINE`
Analyzer showing the input spectrum and the estimated noise floor

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Noise Remover 2.4.0 for Windows (VST3). The current macOS build is version 1.1.3. It uses the spectral path only, because the neural enhancer is Windows-only, and it may differ from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Noise Remover on the dialogue, vocal, or field recording. By default `BASIC` is on and `REDUCTION` is 70%.
Start playback over a passage that contains only noise, such as the pause before the first word, and click `LEARN NOISE`. The plug-in captures the next 0.75 seconds as a noise print.
Adjust `REDUCTION` while listening to the voice. Stop just before consonants, breaths, or room tone start to sound watery.
Switch on only the problems you can actually hear: `LOW RUMBLE`, `50 Hz HUM` or `60 Hz HUM`, `HISS`, or `DIGITAL WHINE`.
If the noise sits in one frequency region, select that range on the analyzer to set the Focus Band.
Use `CLICKS` and `CLIP REPAIR` only on damaged material, and compare with bypass at matched loudness.

ui.caption: An earlier version is shown. In 2.4.0 the switches use the full names in this manual (for example, LOW RUMBLE instead of RUMBLE and CLIP REPAIR instead of DECLIP). The panel also adds the LEARN NOISE and CLEAR PRINT buttons and a Focus Band selection on the analyzer.

Shows the input spectrum (`INPUT`) and the estimated noise floor (`NOISE FLOOR`). The frequency grid is labelled from 32 Hz to 16 kHz and the level scale from 0 to −48 dB. `NO INPUT` appears when no signal arrives. Select a frequency range here to set the Focus Band.
The main cleanup switch and its strength.
Switches for specific problems: `LOW RUMBLE`, `50 Hz HUM`, `60 Hz HUM`, `HISS`, `DIGITAL WHINE`, `CLICKS`, and `CLIP REPAIR`.
Enables the main hybrid cleanup for ambience, air, and room residue. When it is off, the neural path does not run. The target and repair switches still work on their own.

Sets the cleanup strength from natural to maximum reduction. It raises the spectral amount, the reduction depth, and the noise bias together. High values can cause watery artifacts and remove consonants and room tone.
Captures the next 0.75 seconds of noise-only audio and applies that noise print to the cleanup. Playback must be running over a passage that contains only noise.
Clears the learned noise print and returns to the adaptive cleanup.

tip.text: Without a noise print, the cleanup adapts to the noise on its own. Learn a print when the noise is steady and you have a clean noise-only passage of at least 0.75 seconds.

body.p: Focus Band concentrates the reduction on the noise inside a frequency range that you select on the analyzer. Use it when the noise sits in one region, such as a fan whir in the low mids or hiss in the top octaves. The three Focus values are also host parameters, so you can set or automate them from your DAW.

rows: Turns the focused reduction on or off.
Lower edge of the focus band.
Upper edge of the focus band.
A fixed 80 Hz high-pass that removes low-frequency rumble and handling noise. It can also thin out bass and the body of low voices, so compare with bypass.
Removes 50 Hz mains hum and its harmonics.
Removes 60 Hz mains hum and its harmonics.
Reduces steady broadband hiss with a separate high-frequency path that also works when BASIC is off. It overlaps cymbals, sibilance, and air, so start gently.
Suppresses narrow, steady digital whine tones. It cannot always tell a whine from a sustained musical note.
Repairs short clicks and impulse noise from the surrounding waveform. Long clicks and larger damage need manual editing.
Reconstructs clipped, flat-topped waveform peaks. The result is an estimate and cannot recreate the original peak exactly.

body.p: On Windows, `BASIC` combines a neural speech enhancer with spectral restoration. If the neural path cannot run, the plug-in switches to the spectral path so processing continues. When `BASIC` is off, the neural path does not run at all. The macOS build always uses the spectral path. The plug-in reports its processing latency to the host so the track stays aligned.

warn.text: Real-time cleanup cannot restore what is not in the recording. Strong settings remove noise but can also remove consonants, breaths, and room tone. Always compare with bypass at matched loudness.

body.p: Use the arrows to step through presets, or open the list to choose Init or one of your saved presets. Save stores the current settings as a .tbnoiseremoverpreset file. The name shows CUSTOM after you change a setting. Undo and Redo step through recent parameter changes.
Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Dialogue with room tone
recipes.use: Steady room or air-conditioning noise under speech.
steps: Learn the print from the pause before the first word.
Raise REDUCTION until the noise sits under the voice, then back off slightly.

recipes.title: Mains hum
recipes.use: A steady low buzz from power or cabling.
settings: Match the mains frequency where it was recorded
On only if there is also rumble
steps: Mains power is 60 Hz in Korea and North America and 50 Hz in most of Europe.
Try one hum switch at a time. The wrong one makes little difference.

recipes.title: Fan noise in one band
recipes.use: A whir or whine that sits in one frequency region.
steps: Select the range where the noise is strongest on the analyzer.
Narrow the band if the voice starts to change.

recipes.title: Damaged recording
recipes.use: Clicks or clipped peaks in a recording.
steps: Render each repair on its own and compare, so you know which one changed the sound.

rows: The voice sounds watery or swirly.
REDUCTION is too high. Lower it, or learn a new noise print from a cleaner noise-only passage.
The noise print did not help.
The captured 0.75 seconds must contain only noise. Click CLEAR PRINT and learn again from a longer pause.
The bass or the body of the voice is gone.
Turn off LOW RUMBLE or the hum switch and compare.
Cymbals or sibilance lost their air.
Turn off HISS or lower REDUCTION.
With BASIC off, only the switched targets and repairs process the sound.
No signal is reaching the plug-in. Check the track routing and playback.
The macOS build uses the spectral path only, and its version is older.

body.p: LEARN NOISE and CLEAR PRINT are buttons, not host parameters.

rows: Added Focus Band, which concentrates the reduction on a frequency range selected on the analyzer.
Added noise print capture with LEARN NOISE and CLEAR PRINT. The neural path no longer runs while BASIC is off, and the plug-in switches to a safe spectral fallback if the neural path fails.
Moved the effect logo and product name into a shared rack header, and improved previous/next navigation and preset saving and loading.
